title: Introduce RAG scenario sandbox with stubbed backends and living fixtures
author: Maya Singh
description:
Motivation: Make it trivial for engineers to iterate on RAG flows locally without spinning up heavyweight infra. This PR adds a small, curated playground that wires a RAG template (retriever + agent pattern) to a suite of stubbed backends (HTTP mock, in-memory vector index, and a small file-backed document store) plus a set of living fixtures used by the quickstart docs. The goal is developer productivity: fast authoring loops, reproducible smoke checks, and clear examples of how to swap in a production index or connector.

What this PR contains: a) a new quickstart in examples/rag-sandbox/ that includes a lightweight Go-based runner and a Node dev-proxy used for in-browser debugging; b) a set of backend stubs under examples/rag-sandbox/stubs/ (http-mock, simple-kv-index, file-corpus) with documented interfaces so engineers can replace them with a real vector DB or HTTP connector; c) a small telemetry probe harness that emits compact traces and custom events compatible with Redwood Console examples (span names and minimal attributes); d) an authoring README and a docs snippet that will be picked up by the docs site build to show a live-first example.

Checklist: - [x] Add sandbox runner and Node dev-proxy - [x] Implement http-mock + simple in-memory vector index - [x] Add telemetry probe hooks and example traces - [x] Add step-by-step README and quickstart snippet for docs - [x] Add snapshot smoke tests for deterministic replay - [x] CI: add sanity job in examples smoke matrix.

How to run locally: 1) cd examples/rag-sandbox 2) make install (installs dev-proxy and builds go runner) 3) make start (starts http-mock on :8081 and runner on :8080) 4) open http://localhost:3000/playground to interactively exercise retrieval and tool-calling. There are environment toggles to switch from in-memory index to a file corpus or to proxy to a real Redis/FAISS endpoint.

Testing: included deterministic snapshot smoke tests under examples/rag-sandbox/test/snapshots that run the runner against the http-mock and assert stable outputs for the canonical prompt set. CI adds an examples-smoke job that runs on PRs touching examples/**.

Docs/site: small docs fragment examples/rag-sandbox/docs/quickstart.md is authored to be embedded in the docs site. The fragment demonstrates the change from stubbed to production connectors and highlights telemetry signals to watch in Redwood Console.

Notes on scope: this is intentionally small — the sandbox is not a production connector. The interfaces are intentionally explicit to make it straightforward to plumb in the Dedicated/Private connectors in subsequent PRs.

Related: ENG-8921 (developer onboarding flow), PM-431 (quickstart content spec).
